title: Artificial Intelligence for Directors
summary: Plain-language grounding in how machine learning and generative AI are built and deployed, how they differ from rules-based tools, and why they change the firm's risk profile.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Plain-language grounding in how machine learning and generative AI are built and deployed, how they differ from rules-based tools, and why they change the firm's risk profile.
Learning Objectives: Explain how AI systems learn, decide and fail
Distinguish machine learning, generative AI and traditional models, and their risks
Identify where AI is already embedded in the firm, including through vendors
Syllabus: How AI works: data, training, testing and deployment
Machine learning versus generative AI and large language models
Build versus buy: accountability for third-party AI
The vocabulary directors need: drift, bias, hallucination, explainability
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members, especially on risk, audit and technology committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for AI, risk and compliance
Company secretaries and heads of governance supporting board oversight
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No technical background in AI or data science is required.
Core Reading: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, revised 2024)
NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)
FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (2024)
